entries.description: Protocol 1 replicates the original claim that RPMI-7951 and OUMS-23 melanoma cells express elevated basal MAP3K8 compared with A375 cells.
entries.citation_sentence: Johannessen and colleagues first examined basal MAP3K8 expression in multiple cell lines harboring the V600E mutation (Johannessen et al., 2010).
entries.notes: Registered Report protocol; no replication outcome is reported.

entries.description: Protocol 1 replicates the original claim that MAP3K8-expressing RPMI-7951 and OUMS-23 cells maintain ERK and MEK activity despite PLX4720 treatment.
entries.citation_sentence: RPMI-7951 and OUMS-23 cells also exhibited robust, undiminished ERK and MEK activity concomitant with reduced growth sensitivity in the presence of PLX4720 (Figure 3D–E; Johannessen et al., 2010).
entries.notes: Registered Report protocol; no replication outcome is reported.

entries.citation_sentence: RPMI-7951 and OUMS-23 cells also exhibited robust, undiminished ERK and MEK activity concomitant with reduced growth sensitivity in the presence of PLX4720 (Figure 3D–E; Johannessen et al., 2010).

entries.description: Protocol 4 replicates the original claim that MAP3K8 kinase activity is required to regulate MEK and ERK activation in RPMI-7951 cells.
entries.citation_sentence: Finally, in Figure 3I, Johannessen and colleagues determined that MAP3K8 kinase activity is required to regulate MEK/ERK activation in RPMI-7951 cells, findings that further confirm MAP3K8 is an essential upstream activator of the MEK-ERK signaling cascade (George and Salmeron, 2009; Johannessen et al., 2010).
entries.notes: Registered Report protocol; no replication outcome is reported.

entries.original_title: COT drives resistance to RAF inhibition through MAP kinase pathway reactivation
entries.original_authors: Johannessen, CM; Boehm, JS; Kim, SY; Thomas, SR; Wardwell, L; Johnson, LA; Emery, CM; Stransky, N; Cogdill, AP; Barretina, J; Caponigro, G; Hieronymus, H; Murray, RR; Salehi-Ashtiani, K; Hill, DE; Vidal, M; Zhao, JJ; Yang, X; Alkan, O; Kim, S; Harris, JL; Wilson, CJ; Myer, VE; Finan, PM; Root, DE; Roberts, TM; Golub, T; Flaherty, KT; Dummer, R; Weber, BL; Sellers, WR; Schlegel, R; Wargo, JA; Hahn, WC; Garraway, LA
entries.description: Protocol 5 replicates the original claim that combined RAF and MEK inhibition overcomes MAP3K8-driven resistance and reduces viability in MAP3K8-expressing A375 cells.
entries.citation_sentence: As shown in Figures 4E and 4F, both viability and ERK activation was dramatically reduced in MAP3K8-expressing cells treated with either of the combination therapies, similar to cells ectopically expressing MEK1, which remained sensitive to PLX4720 (Johannessen et al., 2010).
entries.notes: Registered Report protocol; no replication outcome is reported.

entries.description: Protocol 5 replicates the original claim that constitutively active MEK1 increases sensitivity to combined BRAF and MEK inhibition with AZD6244 but not with CI-1040.
entries.citation_sentence: Interestingly, overexpression of constitutively active MEK (MEK1[DD]) resulted in increased sensitivity to BRAF inhibition combined with AZD6244, but not CI-1040 (Johannessen et al., 2010).
entries.notes: Registered Report protocol; no replication outcome is reported.
